title: Specify lessons by function, not template
statement: Specify a lesson by the observable functions it must perform, not by a fixed template, so any activity form that keeps each function visible can meet it.
example: One course's lesson contract names 7 observable components that a seminar, document lab, map analysis or writing workshop can each meet.
detail: An AP history course's lesson contract lists seven observable components, from a retrieval task that activates a prerequisite to an exit check that produces an instructional decision. It describes functions and fields rather than page styling, so a seminar, document lab, map analysis, short explanation or writing workshop can meet it if the evidence chain stays visible, and the course's sequencing brief applies the same idea to units. This concerns the form of the activity; the rule that lessons share one interface concerns their controls.
against: The contract sits in a design document since marked historical, and no outcome was measured.

evidence.quote: This does not require every lesson to look identical in an application. The contract describes functions and fields, not CSS. A seminar, document lab, map analysis, short explanation, or writing workshop can satisfy the same handoff if the evidence chain remains visible.
Every lesson must contain the following observable components: ... an exit check that produces an instructional decision.
